entries.note: Core test case. The working hypothesis ('rename keeps the body') gives one continuous body 1542-present, which matches how the Holy See itself narrates it (Integrae servandae recites 1542 and 1908 as its own history). But 1965 is a rename + change of purpose + new 'ordo' at once, and 1917 adds a whole former congregation (Index). The Pope was prefect until 1968 (REU) — CIC 1917 can. 247; Integrae servandae n.2. Competence changes (research): 1908-11-03: Gains all matters of indulgences (doctrine and use); loses ecclesiastical precepts (to Council), election of bishops (to Consistorial), dispensation of religious vows (to Religious). (Pius X, ap. const. Sapienti consilio, 29 Jun 1908, in force 3 Nov 1908, AAS 1 (1909) 7-19); 1917-03-25: Absorbs the Congregation of the Index (new Sectio de Indice); loses indulgences (to Penitentiary, keeps dogmatic aspects). (Benedict XV, m.p. Alloquentes proxime, 25 Mar 1917, AAS 9-I (1917) 167); 1965-12-07: Renamed; purpose recast from defending to promoting doctrine; new procedure for examining books (author to be heard). (Paul VI, m.p. Integrae servandae, 7 Dec 1965, AAS 57 (1965) 952-955); 1966-06-14: Index of Forbidden Books loses force of ecclesiastical law (CDF notification). (CDF notification of 14 Jun 1966); 2019-01-17: Absorbs all tasks of the Pontifical Commission Ecclesia Dei (dedicated section). (Francis, m.p. [Ecclesia Dei] 'Da oltre trent'anni', 17 Jan 2019); 2022-06-05: Pontifical Commission for the Protection of Minors established within it (PE Art. 78); PBC and ITC established within it (PE Art. 77). (Francis, ap. const. Praedicate Evangelium, 19 Mar 2022, in force 5 Jun 2022 (Art. 250)).

founded.note: CE: 'Thus arose an autonomous tribunal ... From the year 1323 we have the first document of a transaction adjudicated collegialiter, and in a definitive way by that, tribunal; John XXII, by the Bull "Ratio Juris" (1331), laid down certain rules for it'; the name 'Rota' 'occurs first in 1336'. Rejected and alternative claims: (a) the vatican.va Rota profile says 'Con Innocenzo IV e il primo Concilio di Lione [1245] i cappellani formarono un tribunale stabile'. It is the main alternative if the owner prefers it. (b) Ratio iuris is dated 1331 by CE and the vatican.va profile, but 1326 by John XXIII's address to the Rota of 19 Oct 1959. It is a regulating act, not a founding act. (c) The 1336 date is for the name only. The 1908 revival is already treated as continuity (H10).
